rationale: The psalm says the speaker counted all his bones while observers looked on; John quotes a bone not being broken. The latter wording is not present here, so this exact fulfillment identification is not established.
The psalm commands eternal gates to rise for the King of glory; Acts describes Jesus lifted into a cloud but names no gates and quotes no such command. This event identification remains uncredited.

The supplied psalm says stronghold, the Lord's name and covenant knowledge; it does not supply the familiar secret or friendship wording. John's statement about friends and disclosed knowledge does not settle that proposed textual link.
Deuteronomy explicitly names Hermon, Sanior and Senir; this psalm instead says the beloved. No exact identification of that expression with a named mountain is established.

Job explicitly describes deer labor and birth pains; the psalm says the voice makes deer ready. A birth interpretation of the supplied wording is not established, so this proposed equivalence is uncredited.

The psalm title names a dedication of the house and David but does not identify the event. Chronicles describes Solomon and the people dedicating God's house; the two are not assigned the same historical occasion.
Keilah is a city with doors and bars in Saul's report, but the psalm's enclosed city is unnamed. The shared enclosure feature does not establish its identity as Keilah.
